title: A Will for the Confession
premise: Insurance investigator Quentin Almeida is hired by a dying woman, Marisol Vane, who pays in advance for him to prove that her husband's murder has not yet happened — a murder she insists will occur at the family's thirtieth anniversary dinner. As Quentin digs into the Vane estate and an unsolved disappearance from thirty years ago, he discovers the 'future' murder mirrors one already committed and buried, with every heir's alibi woven from the same night. When the anniversary dinner arrives, Quentin must choose between protecting the town's carefully filed secrets and forcing a confession the law can no longer touch; in the end, Marisol's will itself becomes the instrument of justice, disinheriting everyone who lied and naming Quentin executor of the truth.
about_author: Lena Quintana spent a decade as a claims adjuster in small-town New England before turning to fiction, where she developed a reputation for mysteries built on paperwork, probate, and quiet menace. She writes from a converted records office and admits she still alphabetizes her research notes.

chapters.title: Paid in Advance
chapters.summary: Quentin Almeida, whose photographic memory keeps the town's secrets neatly filed, takes a strange retainer from Marisol Vane: prove her husband's murder hasn't happened — yet. Through Quentin's POV, we feel his unease as the advance payment signals a client who expects to be dead before delivery. The beat is cold curiosity curdling into dread.

chapters.title: The Anniversary Clause
chapters.summary: Marisol reveals the murder is scheduled for the family's thirtieth anniversary dinner and shows Quentin a clause in her husband's will that triggers if he dies that night. In her POV, we see a woman rehearsing grief for a crime not yet committed. Emotional beat: love twisted into prophecy.

chapters.title: Thirty Years of Alibis
chapters.summary: Quentin cross-references the heirs' alibis and finds they all trace to a single night three decades ago — the night a housekeeper vanished. His memory surfaces a police report he once filed and forgot. POV: Quentin. Beat: the thrill of pattern recognition shadowed by guilt over what he chose not to see.

chapters.title: The Heir Who Smiles
chapters.summary: At the Vane estate, eldest son Theodore charms Quentin while quietly having his office searched. Told partly through Theodore's POV, we watch power perform innocence. Beat: seductive menace — the reader sees the corruption Quentin only suspects.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Kept
chapters.summary: In the estate's basement records, Quentin finds a ledger in the missing housekeeper's handwriting documenting payments, threats, and a second set of books. Her ghost-voiced interludes frame the chapter. Beat: the dead speaking through paper, and Quentin realizing invisibility was her survival strategy too.

chapters.title: A Memory That Lies
chapters.summary: Quentin's perfect recall fails him for the first time — a crucial detail from fifteen years ago contradicts the file, suggesting someone altered records he trusted absolutely. POV alternates between Quentin and Marisol. Beat: vertigo; the investigator's identity cracks open.

chapters.title: Dinner Reservations
chapters.summary: Invitations go out; the heirs converge, each privately pressuring or bribing Quentin, revealing their alibis are coordinated, not coincidental. Ensemble POV through Quentin's observations at a pre-dinner cocktail hour. Beat: rising tension, a locked room assembling itself around him.

chapters.title: The Glass Raised
chapters.summary: The anniversary dinner begins. Toasts are made, a glass shatters, and Marisol collapses — poisoned, but alive, her near-death staged to force the killer's hand. POV shifts rapidly among the table. Climactic beat: the prophecy half-fulfilled, panic unmasking faces.

chapters.title: Confession Outside the Law
chapters.summary: With the statute long expired, Quentin corners the true killer — Marisol herself orchestrated the threat to extract a confession from the person who killed the housekeeper: her husband, still living, whose crime the family covered up. Beat: justice without handcuffs, devastating and quiet.

chapters.title: Executor of the Truth
chapters.summary: Marisol's revised will disinherits every liar and names Quentin executor, tasking him with publishing the housekeeper's ledger. He files his last secret away — then chooses, for the first time, to read it aloud. Final beat: redemption through disclosure; the invisible man steps into the light.
